appraisal_events.evidence: je couvris de baisers fous les joues pleines de tabac de mon vieil oncle ... il est mort bien des années après sans qu'aucun de nous l'ait jamais revu.
appraisal_events.explanation: As a side effect of the rupture between his uncle and his parents, the narrator (as a participant, not merely as narrating voice) permanently loses access to the uncle and the glamorous adult world (the 'dame en rose', talk of artists) he had briefly been admitted to.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator is quietly cut off from his uncle and the fashionable social circle he had glimpsed, a lasting exclusion that lands on him as a participant even though the central blame falls on the uncle.

ambiguities: It is debatable whether the narrator's permanent loss of contact with his uncle counts as a staged social outcome for him as a participant, or is simply a consequence of the already-scored rupture between the father and the uncle, narrated at a distance; scored conservatively with a modest delta and confidence.

'le grand-père du narrateur' is mentioned only as a co-source, alongside the father, of the same violent confrontation with the uncle already captured in the accepted annotation (E1); the passage gives him no distinct local outcome of his own, so he was omitted from scoring.
